latin: Mirabilia artis magicae non sunt nisi per unionem et actuationem eorum quae seminaliter et separate sunt in natura.
translation: The marvels of the magical art come about only through the union and actuation of those things that exist seminally and separately in nature.
translation_note: 'seminaliter et separate' parallels the same pair of terms in 9>5's 'seminaliter et separata', which Farmer's note on 9>5 explicitly links to this thesis (farmer1998:25215).
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch17, from Latin at farmer1998:25272
doctrine: Farmer groups this thesis with 9>10-14, explaining that the purified soul of the magician can gather up the rational forces distributed through the celestial and terrestrial worlds and elevate them, so that the magus functions as a cosmic priest, cross-referencing 8>3 and 10>3 (farmer1998:25295).
historiography: Akopyan (2018) and Akopyan (2021) quote this thesis's Latin verbatim in the same footnote as 9>5, from consecutive pages of Pico's magic conclusions, treating the pair as a matched statement of the magus's power over dispersed seminal virtues (akopyan2018:581; akopyan2021:1339).

quotations.text: Mirabilia artis Magicae non fiunt nisi per unionem et actuationem eorum, quae seminaliter et separatae sunt in natura

not_established: Farmer's fuller discussion of theses 9>10-14, referenced at pp. 131-32 of his study, is not given beyond the note excerpt consulted.
